risk.title: Risk-ON
risk.text: VIX about 15 and S&P 500 near 7,650 after the Fed-day rebound. Breadth is weak: only 31% of stocks sit above their 50-day average.

geo.title: Geopolitical shock: yes, escalating
geo.text: US-Iran war and Hormuz disruption. Ceasefire expired in August, the East-West pipeline shut on 11 Sep, Brent is about $100.

gates.thin: Japan is likely on holiday 21 to 23 Sep and China is closed 25 Sep (calendar, not confirmed by news). Fri 18 Sep was quarterly triple witching.

currencies.why: Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep and 16 of 18 officials see another hike. August payrolls +162k against about 53k expected. Core CPI ran a tick hot. Q2 GDP only 1.5%. Net oil exporter. No CFTC line for the dollar index (it trades on ICE), so COT is scored 0.

RBA at 4.35% after three hikes this year, and another is priced for 29 Sep or November. Trimmed-mean inflation 3.6%. Growth is soft and unemployment rose to 4.5%. Coal and iron ore help. Fast money is net long and adding.

Norges Bank at 4.25%, meeting 24 Sep with new forecasts. A hike is debated for September or December. Inflation is lower than the bank projected. The biggest winner from $100 oil. No CFTC line for the krone, so COT is scored 0.

ECB hiked to 2.50% on 10 Sep and markets price more. Headline inflation 3.3% but core eased to 2.4%. Growth forecasts were upgraded. Energy importer, so the oil shock is a drag. COT is mixed: leveraged funds short but covering, asset managers heavily long. Jobs data not checked yet.

BoE held 3.75% on a 6-3 vote and warns a hike is more likely. CPI 3.1% and rising. Unemployment 4.9% with payrolls falling. Ten-year gilt yield above 5% and fiscal worries under the new government pull the score down. COT is mixed.

BoC held 2.25% with a hawkish lean. Q2 GDP +3.3% annualised and oil helps. But August jobs fell 42k, wages slowed to 2.0%, and new 50% US tariffs hit about C$28bn of goods. Still net short but covering fast.
SNB at 0%, meeting 24 Sep with a hold expected. Q2 GDP +1.9% q/q, the strongest in five years, and CPI 0.8% beat forecasts. Safe-haven bid is weak while VIX is low, and both COT groups are net short.

BoJ hiked to 1.25% on a 7-2 vote and the market read it as not hawkish enough. Japan imports its energy, core CPI is 1.7%, and Q2 GDP was +0.3%. Both COT groups flipped to net long before the decision, which could unwind. Intervention risk is the upside tail.
RBNZ hiked to 2.75% on 2 Sep but sounded cautious and NZD fell. CPI 4.1% (2.9% ex-fuel). Growth is weak, unemployment is high, and Q2 GDP is due next week. COT is neutral.

Riksbank at 1.75%, meeting 24 Sep with a hold expected. CPIF 0.7% is the lowest since 2020 and below forecasts. Adjusted unemployment 8.7%. First hike is seen in November at the earliest. Election result of 13 Sep not checked. No CFTC line for the krona, so COT is scored 0.
